title: Length Rationer: kernel signal fusion and prefill hedging for pad reduction
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: Mixed-production traffic shows heavy variance in request sequence lengths (chat turns, API playgrounds, embedding+metadata requests). Current bucketing and padding introduces significant token-padding waste for medium-length tail requests and reduces overall GPU utilization. Goal: implement a runtime component (Length Rationer) that fuses lightweight kernel selection heuristics with an online sequence-length histogram and a prefill-aware hedging scheduler to reduce padded tokens and improve overall tps while preserving p99 latency SLOs.

Scope and objectives:
- Maintain a per-worker sliding histogram of incoming sequence-lengths and recent latency footprints (50–5k samples, decaying).
- Compute a lightweight kernel "preference score" per sequence-length bucket combining: estimated kernel throughput (tokens/sec), memory pressure (KV-resident ratio), and attention-mode suitability (full vs. sparse/fused attention).
- Use scores to pick kernel / kernel-variant hints and to reorganize micro-batches across 2 runtime pathways: low-latency (short sequences, tight p99) and high-throughput (coalesced medium/long sequences).
- Introduce a prefill hedging policy: detect prefill-heavy bursts and allow speculative prefill-to-decode slot promotion for a small fraction of micro-batches to avoid decode starvation that forces excessive pad-padding later.
- Reduce global pad-percent (percent of padding tokens across GPU) by >= 20% on mixed workloads, maintain p99 generation latency within 1.15x baseline, and increase overall token throughput by >= 8% under production mix.

Design details (high level):
1) Runtime histogram and bucket shrink/grow
   - Keep compact histogram (64 buckets, exponential bucket widths) updated asynchronously, decayed with a half-life ~60s to adapt to diurnal/traffic shifts.
   - Buckets carry weight, observed kernel score averages, and recent reblend count to avoid oscillation.

2) Kernel signal fusion
   - Runtime computes a kernel_signal = w1*throughput_est + w2*(1-memory_pressure) + w3*attention_fit where attention_fit is 1 for short/full attention and 0.8 for sparse-friendly sequences.
   - Throughput_est derived from microbench lookup table (model x seq_len x kernel_variant) updated by nightly offline profiler and runtime microbenchmarks during low traffic windows.
   - Kernel hints emitted as soft preferences; renderer/runtime scheduler retains right to override for hard SLO paths.

3) Prefill hedging scheduler
   - When histogram shows growing prefill tail (prefill_ratio > 0.35 for medium-length buckets) the scheduler can promote up to X% micro-batches to speculative decode slots (configurable, start X=8%).
   - Speculative slots use fast-path kernel variants with smaller memory footprint and slightly lower throughput to reduce per-request pad accumulation.

4) Micro-batch shaping policy
   - Short sequences: prioritized to low-latency pool, kernel_hint favors fused attention kernels and minimal KV shims.
   - Medium/long sequences: packed with variable-padding windows; when packing, allow small sequence trimming (drop trailing padding tokens at packing boundary) if decoding budget permits and if model-compat checks pass.

Telemetry and experiments:
- New metrics emitted: pad_percent, kernel_hint_match_rate, prefill_ratio_by_bucket, speculative_slot_rate, pad_tokens_saved, per-kernel tokens/sec estimates.
- Create a microbench harness that replays 48h of sampled production traffic and measures pad_percent and tokens/sec across baseline, config-A (hedging only), config-B (kernel signal only), and combined config.
- A/B plan: rollout to 5% of Dedicated traffic (low-SLO) for 72h, compare pad_percent and p99 latency; expand to 25% if pad_pct improves and p99 <= 1.15x baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- pad_percent reduction >= 20% on replayed mixed traffic trace (staging).
- p99 generation latency <= 1.15x baseline on 95% of test slices.
- kernel_hint_match_rate >= 80% for top-3 kernels in the night profiler table.
- No observable increase in generation errors or quality regressions in eval prompt set.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Overaggressive hedging can increase tail latency if speculative slots are misused; mitigated by conservative X% and fail-open defaults.
- Kernel hint inaccuracies can cause suboptimal throughput; we keep soft hints and a fast fallback path to original kernel.
- Additional runtime complexity increases maintenance cost; plan incremental rollout and monitor metrics closely.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1 (spike): implement histogram + offline profiler integration, design kernel_signal formula and config knobs. (Aisha, Daniel)
- Week 2: implement kernel_hint plumbing and a simple selector that labels micro-batches; add telemetry. (Daniel)
- Week 3: implement prefill hedging scheduler and micro-batch reshaping routines; add unit tests and microbench harness. (Aisha)
- Week 4: staging run with 48h replay, iterate on weights w1..w3, and run canary 5% Dedicated traffic. (team)
- Post-canary: roll to 25% then 100% Dedicated after sanity checks.

Open questions:
- How to best measure attention_fit for models with KV-size dependent sparse support? (Research may provide model capabilities table)
- Parameterize decay half-life per-customer? (some customers have highly bursty traffic)
